Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has continued to expand at a solid pace, but the Committee’s focus on the lack of further progress toward 2 percent highlights the inflation persistence emphasized in New Keynesian Phillips-curve frameworks (Calvo pricing; Woodford) and the welfare costs of above-target inflation documented in the literature (Dotsey; Ireland; Prescott). Keeping the federal funds rate at 5.25–5.50 percent and signaling no cuts until “greater confidence” is consistent with inflation-forecast targeting (Svensson) and with addressing inflationary bias under discretionary policy, while the slower balance-sheet runoff (reducing Treasury redemptions from $60B to $25B) is a modestly less restrictive adjustment that can ease pressures along the term structure. Net tone: growth-positive but inflation-cautious, with a slight dovish tilt from the QT slowdown but overall restrictive stance maintained.
